issues.display_title: Issue #312: Canvas editor: render doors green and windows blue
issues.main_description_html:
Assignee: Muhamad Rifky — Developer

Implementation task for #311.

Context

In the canvas editor, doors and windows render as near-identical grey lines. They are not hard-coded grey — their colors come from theme tokens at src/lib/newEditor/editor/palette.ts:31:

C.door = tokenRGB("--chart-2"); C.win = tokenRGB("--chart-4");

and in this theme both tokens are achromatic: --chart-2: oklch(0.556 0 0), --chart-4: oklch(0.371 0 0) (zero chroma = pure grey, in both the light and dark variants — see globals.css:76,78,114,116). Request: doors green, windows blue.

Scope

  • In palette.ts, point C.door at a green and C.win at a blue
  • Both must read on light and dark backdrops — refresh() re-resolves on theme switch, so either branch per theme or pick values that hold up on both
  • Follow the existing precedent at palette.ts:40: C.shapeFill/C.shapeStroke are already fixed (non-token) colors with a comment explaining why — same pattern applies here unless design mints --editor-door / --editor-window tokens

What NOT to touch

  • Every 2D consumer already routes through C.door / C.win — draw.ts:83-137 (strokes, selected/hot states via doorSel/winSel) and draw.ts:400 (add-tool preview). No per-call-site edits needed.
  • 3D needs nothing: scene3d.ts renders doors/windows as holes cut into walls (wallOpenings), not colored geometry. There is no door/window color in 3D.
  • C.doorSel/C.doorHot/C.winSel/C.winHot stay mapped to selection/hover tokens — only the resting colors change.

Acceptance criteria

  • Doors render green, windows blue, in both light and dark themes
  • Selected/hovered doors and windows keep the existing selection/hover treatment
  • Add-door / add-window tool previews match the new colors (draw.ts:400 inherits automatically)
  • npx tsc --noEmit clean, eslint clean, vitest green

Open question

Exact green/blue values are a design call — the screenshot in #311 shows intent, not specific colors. If design has values, use them; otherwise pick a pair with adequate contrast on both themes and flag them for review in the PR.

issues.display_title: Issue #319: Editor: rename fp_history localStorage key and clear it on leaving editor/preview
issues.main_description_html:
Context

analisa key localStorage on the editor turned up the per-level undo/redo cache written by src/lib/newEditor/editor/history.ts.

Two problems:

  1. Key format inconsistent. History used fp_history_{level_id} (underscore) while the wizard blob uses gothru_wizard:{projectId} (colon). Colon is the better separator — level ids are nanoids, so the underscore form is ambiguous to grep and to prefix-match.
  2. Never cleaned up. No removeItem for that prefix existed anywhere in the repo. Deleting a level or a project left its stacks behind permanently. Each entry holds up to 40 undo + 40 redo full-model JSON snapshots (walls, doors, windows, icons, roomNames, manualAreas, shapes, roomHeights), so a busy session can push the origin toward the ~5MB localStorage quota on its own. Both saveHistory and the wizard autosave swallow quota errors silently, so a full quota kills wizard autosave with no user-visible signal.

Scope

  • Change key format to fp_history:{level_id}.
  • Clear fp_history* when the user leaves the editor and when they leave preview.
  • Leave the wizard blob (gothru_wizard*) alone — it should survive leaving the editor.
  • Leave pre-existing legacy fp_history_* entries alone at load time (no migration); the exit sweep removes them incidentally.
  • Rename ClearWizardCacheOnLeave → ClearEditorHistoryOnLeave, since it no longer touches wizard cache.

Acceptance criteria

  • History persists and restores under fp_history:{level_id}
  • Leaving /editor or /preview removes all fp_history* keys
  • Navigating editor ⇄ preview does not wipe history (round trip keeps undo)
  • gothru_wizard*, gf_project_id, mapthru_editor_split, theme survive the sweep
  • Typecheck, lint, tests green

RESULT

Commit: fef8777 · PR: #320 · Branch: feature/319-fp-history-key-cleanup (cut from development @ 9e0aad2)

What changed

File Change
src/lib/newEditor/editor/history.ts histStorageKey: fp_history_${k} → fp_history:${k}
src/components/editor/ClearEditorHistoryOnLeave.tsx Renamed from ClearWizardCacheOnLeave.tsx; sweep loop extracted to exported clearEditorStorage(), now matching prefix fp_history only
src/app/preview/layout.tsx Mounts ClearEditorHistoryOnLeave so leaving preview sweeps too
src/app/editor/layout.tsx Import + usage updated for the rename
src/components/editor/__tests__/clearEditorStorage.test.ts New — pins what the sweep deletes vs keeps
src/lib/newEditor/__tests__/history-storage.test.ts New — loadHistory reads the colon form, ignores the legacy one

6 files, +113 / −9.

Decisions taken during implementation

  • gothru_wizard* no longer swept on editor exit. It previously was — this is a deliberate behavior change requested mid-implementation, so a wizard draft now survives leaving the editor.
  • No load-time migration of legacy fp_history_*. Cross-refresh undo is a convenience, not data worth migrating. The exit sweep's prefix match clears the old form incidentally.
  • Editor ⇄ preview does not wipe history. pendingResetTimer is module-level, so whichever layout mounts cancels the other's pending sweep. Only leaving both routes for good fires it — same mechanism that already guarded against React Strict Mode's synthetic unmount.

Acceptance criteria

  • History persists and restores under fp_history:{level_id} — covered by history-storage.test.ts
  • Leaving /editor or /preview removes all fp_history* keys — clearEditorStorage.test.ts + component mounted in both layouts
  • Navigating editor ⇄ preview does not wipe history — by module-level timer cancellation; not unit-tested, needs manual check
  • gothru_wizard*, gf_project_id, mapthru_editor_split, theme survive the sweep — asserted in clearEditorStorage.test.ts
  • Typecheck, lint, tests green — see below

Verification

  • npx tsc --noEmit — clean
  • npx eslint on all six touched files — clean
  • npx vitest run — 335 passed, 3 skipped; 2 test files failing

The 2 failing files are pre-existing and unrelated: roundtrip-firstedit.test.ts and mappedin-editor/convert.test.ts both ENOENT on fixture files absent from the repo (new-ui/new-editor/public/sample.txt, samples/sample2-txt/a.txt). Confirmed by stashing this branch's changes and re-running on a clean tree — identical 2 files / 1 test fail there (333 passed vs 335 here, the delta being this branch's 2 new tests).

Left for the tester

Browser check not performed — unit tests only:

  1. Editor → make edits → navigate to preview → back to editor → undo still works
  2. Then leave to dashboard → fp_history* gone from localStorage, gothru_wizard* still present

issues.display_title: Issue #316: Block owner-only project actions for collaborators
issues.main_description_html:
Problem

In the project list, a collaborator (a user a project was shared with) can click Publish, Unpublish, and Delete. The backend restricts all three to the project owner (403 forbidden in action/v1/project/publish.go, unpublish.go, delete.go), so the actions always fail — the UI just does not say why.

The list API already reports ownership: is_owner in the project response (action/v1/project/shared.go). The frontend was not reading it.

Scope

  • Read is_owner from the project payload on the frontend.
  • Keep the owner-only actions visible and clickable.
  • On click by a non-owner, open an info modal explaining the action is owner-only, and do not send the request.
  • Same guard on the preview navbar (Publish / Unpublish), which is the sibling caller of the same endpoints.

Acceptance criteria

  • Collaborator clicking Publish / Unpublish / Delete sees an English info modal and no request is sent.
  • Owner behaviour is unchanged (confirm modal → request).
  • Preview navbar Publish / Unpublish behave the same way.
  • Typecheck and lint pass.

Notes

Backend needs no change — it already returns is_owner and rejects non-owners with 403.

RESULT

Frontend-only fix; the backend already returned is_owner and rejected non-owners with 403.

What changed

  • src/actions/projects.ts — Project type gains is_owner?: boolean. Missing value (older payloads, local mock route) is treated as owner.
  • src/components/preview/PreviewConfirmDialog.tsx — new NotOwnerDialog export, built on the existing PreviewModal shell, single "Got it" button. Message: "Only the project owner can do this — this project was shared with you as a collaborator, so you can view and edit it, but you cannot {publish|unpublish|delete} it."
  • src/components/dashboard/ProjectViews.tsx — Publish / Unpublish / Delete stay visible and clickable. openModal() is the single gate: for a non-owner it opens the info modal and no request is sent.
  • src/components/preview/PreviewTopbar.tsx — same guard on the preview navbar's Publish / Unpublish, the sibling caller of the same endpoints.

Acceptance criteria

  • Collaborator clicking Publish / Unpublish / Delete sees an English info modal and no request is sent.
  • Owner behaviour unchanged (confirm modal → request).
  • Preview navbar Publish / Unpublish behave the same way.
  • Typecheck and lint pass (npx tsc --noEmit, npx eslint on the touched files).

issues.display_title: Issue #340: Editor sidebar: list imported panoramas in the object list
issues.main_description_html:
Assignee: Ibnu Rizqia Ramadan — Developer

Problem

The editor sidebar's unified object list has a "Panoramas" category (objectFilters.tsx, objectRows.ts reads level.panoramas), but imported panoramas do not show up — the category count stays 0 even after panoramas have been imported into the project (see the Objects filter dropdown).

Scope

  • Show every imported panorama of the active level as rows in the sidebar object list, under the Panoramas category, with the correct count in the filter dropdown.
  • Cover the import paths that store panoramas (level.panoramas — PanoramaMarker[] from the Add Panorama / TourMkr flow) so the list reflects what is actually on the map.
  • Row behavior consistent with the other categories (select/hover parity where applicable).

Acceptance criteria

  • After importing panoramas, the Panoramas filter shows the correct count and lists each panorama by name.
  • Selecting a panorama row behaves like other object rows (highlight/locate on the map).
  • Empty state unchanged when the level has no panoramas.
  • Typecheck, lint, tests pass.

RESULT

Root cause — the Add Panorama import creates a Point + pano-linked Information (AddPanoramaButton.tsx), not level.panoramas entries. level.panoramas is a legacy field nothing writes (documented in src/lib/map/object-markers.ts), and the sidebar counted/listed Panoramas only from that field — so the filter always showed 0 while the imported panos sat under Points.

What changed

  • src/lib/editor/objectRows.ts — EditorObject gains a pano flag, set by buildEditorObjects via a hasPanoInfo(infoId) resolver. New isPanoObject drives the Panoramas filter: count and rows include pano-linked objects while they keep their own type (a pano-linked point still counts under Points; All counts it once).
  • src/components/editor/panel/ObjectSection.tsx — resolves hasPanoInfo from informationRecords (Information.pano) and feeds it to buildEditorObjects.
  • src/components/editor/panel/SimpleAnnotationList.tsx — the Panoramas per-type list derives rows from pano-linked points/shapes/safety (name from the linked Information, hidden pins dimmed), plus any own level.panoramas markers should the field ever hold data.
  • src/lib/editor/__tests__/objectRows.test.ts — new cases: pano-linked point counts under both Points and Panoramas, All counts once, panorama filter returns it, and legacy no-resolver behavior is unchanged.

Verification — tsc --noEmit clean, vitest 360 passed, eslint clean on changed files.

Addendum (c872c89) — hovering a sidebar row now locates the annotation on the canvas, matching the wall/door/area lists:

  • src/lib/newEditor/editor/index.ts — new engine API hoverAnnotationAt(kind, id) / clearAnnotationHover() driving the existing hoverAnno state.
  • src/lib/newEditor/editor/draw.ts — a hovered point/safety pin gets the selected emphasis (bigger, accent stroke) plus the name tag, so the hover reads on the canvas.
  • src/components/editor/panel/SimpleAnnotationList.tsx — point/safety/panorama rows fire the hover (rows carry annoKind; shapes have no engine hover yet); rows get a hover background.

issues.display_title: Issue #341: Dashboard: refresh Recent tiles after delete and publish toggle (bug #333)
issues.main_description_html:
Assignee: Ibnu Rizqia Ramadan — Developer

Fix task for bug #333 (deleted project still appearing in the dashboard Recent tiles).

Root cause

The backend is correct: project delete is a GORM soft delete and /v1/projects/recent automatically excludes soft-deleted rows. The bug is in the dashboard hook src/app/dashboard/useDashboard.ts: the recent state is fetched only once on mount (load()); handleDelete refreshes the All-projects list and counts but never refetches recent, so a deleted project's tile stays in Recent until a full page reload. handlePublishToggle has the same gap — the status chip on a Recent tile goes stale after publish/unpublish.

Scope

  • Refetch listRecentProjects() after delete and after publish/unpublish in useDashboard.ts.

Acceptance criteria

  • Deleting a project removes its tile from Recent without a page reload.
  • Publishing/unpublishing updates the status chip on the Recent tile without a reload.
  • Typecheck, lint, tests pass.

RESULT

No FE code change needed — the original diagnosis was wrong. useDashboard.ts already optimistically removes deleted/publish-toggled projects from its Recent state, and both listProjects / listRecentProjects server actions fetch with cache: "no-store".

The real root cause is backend: /v1/projects/recent did not filter is_complete = true while the All-projects list does, so abandoned wizard drafts kept appearing as Recent tiles. Fixed in GoThruMedia/Gothru-3d-Floormap-API-GO#97 (commit ea37239, merged to BE development as d6bca8e). Verify on the dashboard once the backend deploys.
